title: Derivation of a size-based smoltification reaction norm for wild Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar)
content:
Abstract
Size and age at smoltification are key life-history traits in Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), influencing marine survival, age at maturation, and reproductive output. However, smolt age data are unavailable for many populations, whereas parr length measurements from routine electrofishing surveys are widely collected. We developed a simplified framework to estimate size-based smoltification reaction norms from parr and smolt length distributions and used these to predict smolt age and length distributions. The framework was applied to five Swedish Baltic salmon rivers spanning a broad latitudinal gradient. River-specific reaction norm parameters were estimated by fitting predicted smolt length distributions to observed data and were subsequently used to predict smolt age distributions. Model performance was evaluated by comparing predicted and observed smolt age and length distributions within rivers and by testing the transferability of reaction norm parameters among rivers. The model reproduced observed smolt length distributions in all five rivers and accurately predicted smolt age distributions in four of the five rivers. Reaction norm parameters were largely transferable among the four northern rivers, producing accurate cross-river predictions of both smolt age and length distributions. In contrast, predictions for the southernmost river, Mörrumsån, were less accurate, suggesting that additional biological processes influence smoltification in this population. The proposed framework provides a practical approach for estimating smolt age and length distributions from routinely collected monitoring data. Because the method relies primarily on parr length data and transferable reaction norm parameters, it has potential to improve the biological realism of Atlantic salmon stock assessments in rivers where direct smolt age data are unavailable.
